summary: INQPORT is an online CICS program that handles a Portfolio Position Inquiry. When invoked, it initialises working storage and copies the passed communication area (DFHCOMMAREA), then reads the customer's position record from the POSFILE VSAM file via CICS, keyed by the account number. If a position is found it formats and sends the position details to the user's screen using CICS map POSMAP (mapset INQSET); if none is found it returns a 'Position not found' message to the caller. A CICS HANDLE CONDITION traps errors and not-found conditions, routing to dedicated error and not-found paragraphs that place a descriptive message (and, for errors, the response code) back into the communication area before returning control. Error conditions handled: record not found (NOTFND) and general access errors (ERROR).

paragraphs.name: MAINLINE
paragraphs.pseudocode:
-- Program driver (runs first)
CALL P100-INIT-PROGRAM        -- set up
CALL P200-GET-POSITION        -- read the position record
IF position exists THEN
  CALL P300-FORMAT-DISPLAY    -- show it on screen
ELSE
  CALL P900-NOT-FOUND        -- report 'not found'
END IF
CICS RETURN TO caller

annotations.note: PERFORM ... THRU is used for every call — an unstructured COBOL idiom; each range is one logical sub-routine.

paragraphs.notes: The mainline (statements after PROCEDURE DIVISION, before the first named paragraph) is the true entry driver even though it is unnamed.

paragraphs.name: P100-INIT-PROGRAM
paragraphs.pseudocode:
CLEAR WS-POSITION-RECORD          -- MOVE LOW-VALUES: blank the record buffer
SET WS-COMMAREA = DFHCOMMAREA     -- copy the caller's comm-area into working storage
CICS HANDLE CONDITION:
  on ERROR  -> jump to P999-ERROR-ROUTINE
  on NOTFND -> jump to P900-NOT-FOUND

annotations.note: CICS HANDLE CONDITION registers implicit jumps that fire automatically on later CICS errors/not-found — control-flow that is not visible as a normal PERFORM.

paragraphs.name: P100-EXIT
paragraphs.pseudocode: EXIT paragraph  -- structured exit point for the P100 THRU range

paragraphs.name: P200-GET-POSITION
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SET position_account (in WS-POSITION-RECORD) = ws_commarea_account_no   -- the key to read by
CICS READ file POSFILE
  KEY: position_account
  INTO: WS-POSITION-RECORD
  RESPONSE CODE -> ws_response_code
IF ws_response_code = NORMAL THEN
  SET POSITION-EXISTS = true    -- record found
ELSE
  SET NO-POSITION = true        -- record not found
END IF
branches: IF WS-RESPONSE-CODE = DFHRESP(NORMAL)  -> POSITION-EXISTS else NO-POSITION

annotations.note: CICS READ (not a plain COBOL READ) — this is online VSAM access through CICS; the RESP field carries the success/fail code instead of AT END.

paragraphs.name: P200-EXIT
paragraphs.pseudocode: EXIT paragraph  -- structured exit point for the P200 THRU range

paragraphs.name: P300-FORMAT-DISPLAY
paragraphs.pseudocode:
CICS SEND MAP POSMAP (mapset INQSET)
  FROM: WS-POSITION-RECORD
  ERASE the screen first
  RESPONSE CODE -> ws_response_code
-- sends the retrieved position data to the user's 3270 screen

annotations.note: RESP(WS-RESPONSE-CODE) is captured here but never checked in this paragraph — a send failure would go unhandled locally (the outer HANDLE CONDITION may still catch it).

paragraphs.name: P300-EXIT
paragraphs.pseudocode: EXIT paragraph  -- structured exit point for the P300 THRU range

paragraphs.name: P900-NOT-FOUND
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SET inqcom_error_msg (in WS-COMMAREA) = 'Position not found for account'
SET DFHCOMMAREA = WS-COMMAREA    -- hand the error message back to the caller
paragraphs.notes: Reached either from the mainline ELSE branch or automatically via the NOTFND HANDLE CONDITION.

paragraphs.name: P900-EXIT
paragraphs.pseudocode: EXIT paragraph  -- structured exit point for the P900 THRU range

paragraphs.name: P999-ERROR-ROUTINE
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SET inqcom_error_msg (in WS-COMMAREA) = 'Error accessing position data'
SET inqcom_response_code (in WS-COMMAREA) = ws_response_code
SET DFHCOMMAREA = WS-COMMAREA    -- hand the error details back to the caller

annotations.note: Reached automatically via the ERROR HANDLE CONDITION registered in P100, not by a normal PERFORM.

paragraphs.name: P999-EXIT
paragraphs.pseudocode: EXIT paragraph  -- structured exit point for the P999 THRU range
